title: Cross-Spectral Reservoir Correlations as a Resource for Finite-Time Quantum Otto Engines
authors: Siddhartha Dutta, Sujay Mondal, Ankush Das, Anumita Mukhopadhyay, Abhijit Bandyopadhyay
abstract: We investigate the thermodynamic consequences of longitudinal-transverse cross-spectral reservoir correlations in a finite-time quantum Otto engine with a two-level working medium. Each reservoir couples through excitation-relaxation and dephasing channels whose fluctuations are characterized by a Hermitian positive-semidefinite spectral-density matrix, with the off-diagonal elements encoding their cross correlations. The finite-time isochoric dynamics is derived within the second-order time-convolutionless framework, without imposing the Markov limit at the outset, so that finite reservoir-memory effects can enter through time-dependent dissipative and reservoir-induced coherent contributions. The resulting dynamics is then recast in Bloch-vector form to construct the stroke-resolved cycle dynamics. At fixed auto-spectral densities, cross-spectral correlations modify the populations and coherences of the working medium and thereby its thermodynamic performance. Increasing the correlation strength can enhance the output power, with the enhancement controlled by the cross-spectral phase and characteristic frequency scale. The correlations also reshape the transient cycle-to-cycle evolution and the approach to periodic operation, while the limit-cycle efficiency remains fixed at the Otto value for the population-preserving unitary strokes considered here. These results establish off-diagonal reservoir spectra as an additional resource for controlling finite-time quantum thermal machines.
summary: This work explores how engineered cross-correlations in the environment reservoirs can enhance the power output of a quantum Otto engine operating in finite time. By using advanced non-Markovian quantum dynamics techniques, the authors demonstrate that these off-diagonal spectral correlations provide a novel control knob for quantum thermal machines. This establishes a new resource for controlling transient energy conversion processes.
main_problem: The paper investigates how longitudinal-transverse cross-spectral reservoir correlations affect the thermodynamic performance of a quantum Otto engine operating in finite time.
main_result: Cross-spectral correlations act as an additional resource, capable of enhancing the output power of the engine, although they do not alter the limit-cycle efficiency.
method: The dynamics are derived using the second-order time-convolutionless (TCL2) framework, which retains non-Markovian, finite-time reservoir memory effects.
model_or_system: The system is a two-level working medium coupled to two bosonic reservoirs (hot and cold) forming a quantum Otto engine. The coupling channels are characterized by a spectral-density matrix including cross-correlation terms.
key_observables: Output power, cycle work, population imbalance ($\langle\sigma_zangle$), and efficiency ($\eta$).
important_parameters: Cross-spectral correlation strength, cross-spectral phase, characteristic frequency scale, and cycle duration ($	au_{cyc}$).
main_assumptions: The analysis avoids the Markov limit to capture finite reservoir memory effects, and the limit-cycle efficiency is fixed at the classical Otto value for the considered unitary strokes.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the finite-time quantum Otto cycle sequence and show the time evolution of the population imbalance ($\langle\sigma_zangle$) over successive cycles, demonstrating sensitivity to cross-correlation strength.
paper_structure: The paper establishes the theoretical framework by analyzing the reservoir coupling via spectral density matrices, derives the non-Markovian dynamics using TCL2, and then applies this to the Otto cycle to quantify the enhancement of power via cross-correlations.
why_interesting: It provides a concrete, controllable mechanism (off-diagonal reservoir spectra) to engineer quantum thermal machines beyond simple temperature or coupling strength variations, which is highly relevant for open quantum systems theory.

figures.caption: Figure 1: Illustration of a finite-time quantum Otto cycle:The two-level working medium S exchanges heat with the hot and cold reservoirs during the isochoric strokes, while the energy-level spacing of its bare Hamiltonian HS is held fixed at ωh and ωc, respectively, with ωh > ωc. Here, Qh denotes the heat absorbed from the hot reservoir, whereas Qc denotes the heat released to the cold reservoir. During each isochore, the system–reservoir coupling also induces a Lamb-shift correction H(α) LS (t) to the bare working-medium Hamiltonian. The isolated expansion and compression strokes vary the bare level spacing as ωh →ωc and ωc →ωh, respectively.
Figure 2: Schematic representation of the finite-time quantum Otto cycle, with the working- medium states (ρS)1, (ρS)2, (ρS)3, and (ρS)4 defined at the boundaries between successive strokes.

Corresponding hot-reservoir parameters are fixed at rh = 1, ω(h) corr = 5, ϕh = π/2. The cycle duration is τcyc = 8 with τh = τc = τexp = τcomp = 2. All remaining are parameters fixed as specified in the text.

Figure 4: Cycle-resolved work to heat ratio η for pure-dephasing and pure-amplitude-damping reservoirs, compared with reservoirs possessing longitudinal–transverse cross-spectral corre- lations of strengths rc = rh = 0.5 and 1. All remaining parameters are fixed as specified in the text.
